learning_outcomes.text: Identify and describe basic principles and methods of the mechanical engineering field.
Explain basic principles of elasticity theory and resistance criteria applicable to mechanical elements.
Explain and interpret theoretical and experimental results, technical documentation, phenomena, and processes in mechanical engineering.
Possess in-depth knowledge of compound stress theories: compound stresses (bending with torsion), torsion, buckling, fatigue, shock, and buckling.
Possess knowledge of analytical and numerical methods for stress and deformation analysis.
Understand the conditions for transitioning from the elastic to the plastic domain and how to evaluate resistance.
Understand the applicability of strength of materials in the design and optimization of mechanical equipment and structures.
Operate with basic methods and techniques in the field and associate them with specific graphical representations in mechanical engineering.
Apply criteria, evaluation methods, concepts, and theories/programs in the design of mechanical systems.
Perform resistance calculations for complex mechanical elements and structures.
Identify and analyze critical areas in structures and mechanisms, proposing improvement solutions.
Apply strength of materials concepts in interdisciplinary mechanical engineering projects.
Select and analyze specific bibliographic sources in mechanical engineering.
Demonstrate autonomy in learning specific mechanical engineering issues.
Resolve independently technical problems specific to strength of materials applicable in mechanical engineering.
Integrate resistance analysis results into the design, testing, and operation of mechanical equipment.
Adopt a proactive attitude for continuous learning and adaptation to new materials and technologies in the field.

syllabus_topics: Fundamental notions of elasticity theory. Calculation relations for physical quantities necessary for expressing failure theories.
Theories and failure criteria applied in mechanical engineering.
Calculation for compound stresses applied to straight, bent, or curved bars.
Torsion of straight bars with arbitrary cross-section.
Calculation of thin-walled rotation vessels.
Calculation of thick-walled cylindrical tubes.
Calculation of rotating discs of constant thickness.
Calculation of straight bars under shock loads.
Notions regarding the calculation of parts stressed in the plastic domain of their material.
Loading of straight bars by forces inclined to their principal axes.
Resistance calculation for eccentrically loaded straight bars.
Resistance calculation for bent bars (frames).
Resistance calculation for plane bars with curved axes.
Torsion of non-circular cross-section bars.
Calculation of thin-walled revolution vessels.
Calculation of thick-walled cylindrical tubes.
Calculation of rotating discs of constant thickness.
Resistance calculation for bars with shock loads.
Recapitulation problems for the exam.
Presentation of laboratory works and occupational safety regulations.
Resistive electrical strain gauging: verifying measurement precision.
Experimental determination of elastic constants for a homogeneous and isotropic material.
Study of the stress state in a straight beam subjected to oblique bending.
Study of the stress state in a closed rectangular frame, subjected to three-point bending.
Study of the stress state in the critical section of a circular bar with a small radius of curvature.
Make-up sessions for missed laboratory works.
teaching_methods: Interactive lectures with explanations on the board
Seminars involving solving applications on the board with student participation
Lectures and explanations for fundamental concepts
Applicative exercises for consolidation and understanding
Case studies and learning for critical thinking and creativity
assessment_rules: The final evaluation result considers the scores and weights allocated to each activity. Grades are integer values from 1 to 10. A grade of 5 certifies the acquisition of minimum learning outcomes and the allocation of study credits. The minimum grade for the Exam, Seminar, and Laboratory components is 5. All laboratory works must be completed, with only one make-up session permitted for a missed laboratory work.
